subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Responding to an OCR-set starting point

questions.q: What is the name of OCR's Component 02 in GCSE (9-1) Art & Design (J170)?
questions.explain: Component 02 is the Externally Set Task, in which candidates respond to a starting point set by OCR.

questions.q: Who sets the starting points that candidates respond to in Component 02?
options: The head of the art department
questions.explain: The task is 'externally set', meaning OCR provides the starting points rather than the centre.

questions.q: What proportion of the overall GCSE marks does Component 02 contribute?
questions.explain: The Externally Set Task is weighted at 40% of the qualification, with the Portfolio (Component 01) worth 60%.

questions.q: From which date is the OCR Externally Set Task early-release paper made available to candidates?
options: 1 January of the year of the exam
1 March of the year of the exam
1 May of the year of the exam
questions.explain: OCR releases the EST starting points from 1 January, allowing an extended preparatory period before the supervised time.

questions.q: How many of the starting points on the OCR-set paper should a candidate develop a response to?
questions.explain: Candidates choose a single starting point from the paper and develop a sustained response to it.

questions.q: Why does OCR provide a range of different starting points rather than a single set task?
options: To allow candidates to choose one that suits their personal interests and strengths
To require candidates to answer every one
To make the task easier to mark
To reduce the amount of preparation needed
questions.explain: Offering several starting points lets each candidate select a theme that best supports a personal and meaningful response.

questions.q: How many assessment objectives are used to assess Component 02?
questions.explain: Component 02 is assessed against the same four assessment objectives (AO1-AO4) as the Portfolio.

questions.q: Which assessment objective focuses on presenting a personal and meaningful response that realises intentions?
questions.explain: AO4 requires candidates to present a personal, meaningful response demonstrating understanding of visual language.

questions.q: A candidate is given a starting point titled 'Fragments'. Which is the strongest opening response?
options: Copying an image of broken glass found online without comment
Investigating relevant artists and gathering first-hand sources connected to the idea of fragments
Beginning the final outcome immediately in the supervised session
Choosing a completely unrelated theme they prefer
questions.explain: A strong response begins by investigating sources and artists (AO1) relevant to the chosen starting point.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the preparatory studies in Component 02?
options: To replace the final outcome entirely
To develop and refine ideas that lead towards the final outcome
To be completed only during the supervised time
To be marked separately from the final piece
questions.explain: Preparatory studies allow candidates to research, experiment and develop ideas before producing the final outcome.

questions.q: How much time is allowed for the preparatory period before the supervised sessions?
options: There is no set time limit on preparation
questions.explain: The preparatory period is unrestricted, giving candidates ample time to develop ideas before the supervised time.

questions.q: Which assessment objective is most directly evidenced by experimenting with and selecting appropriate media and techniques in preparatory work?
questions.explain: AO2 concerns refining work by exploring ideas and experimenting with appropriate media, materials and techniques.

questions.q: Which assessment objective is best met by recording ideas, observations and insights as the preparatory work progresses?
questions.explain: AO3 requires recording ideas, observations and insights relevant to intentions as work develops.

questions.q: Can preparatory studies be brought into and referred to during the supervised sessions?
options: No, all materials are removed beforehand
Yes, the preparatory work informs and supports the final outcome
Only if the teacher completes them
Only digital preparatory work is allowed
questions.explain: Candidates use their preparatory studies during the supervised time to inform and guide the final outcome.

questions.q: During preparation a candidate has strong research but has only worked in pencil. What would most improve their AO2 evidence?
options: Experimenting with a range of media such as paint, print and collage
Repeating the same pencil study several times
questions.explain: AO2 rewards exploration and experimentation with a variety of appropriate media and techniques.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised time are allowed to produce the final outcome in Component 02?
questions.explain: OCR allows 10 hours of supervised time for candidates to produce their final outcome.

questions.q: What is the main condition governing the production of the final outcome?
options: It may be completed at home over several weeks
It must be produced under supervised conditions within the set time
It can be made by a group of candidates together
questions.explain: The final outcome is created under supervised conditions during the allocated supervised time.

questions.q: How does the final outcome relate to the preparatory studies?
options: It should be unrelated to the preparation
It should realise the intentions developed through the preparatory work
It should simply repeat one preparatory study exactly
It replaces the need for any preparation
questions.explain: The final outcome brings together and realises the ideas and intentions built up during preparation.

questions.q: In the supervised session a candidate realises their planned composition is too ambitious for the time available. What is the best course of action?
options: Abandon the starting point and begin a new theme
Adapt and focus the plan so a resolved outcome can be completed in the time
Continue exactly as planned and leave it unfinished
Complete the rest at home after the session
questions.explain: Managing time to produce a resolved outcome within the supervised period supports AO4, while home completion is not permitted.

specSource: OCR GCSE (9–1) Art & Design (J170) specification; Component 02: Externally Set Task
